2025_133_course_description_book_2024_20.paragraph: The Troy School District's 2025-2026 Course Descriptions booklet catalogs the courses offered at Athens High School and Troy High School, issued under Dr. Richard Machesky, Superintendent of Schools, and marked "Revised, February, 2025." It opens with the district's Title IX and Section 504/ADA nondiscrimination policy, sets out graduation requirements and flexibility options, describes courses department by department with course numbers, grade levels, credits and prerequisites, and closes with Oakland Schools Technical Campus information and the anti-discrimination grievance procedure. The governing requirement stated throughout is that all students must earn 22.5 total credits to be eligible for a Troy High School or Troy Athens diploma.
2025_133_course_description_book_2024_20.page:
**Publication**
2025-2026 Course Descriptions for Athens High School and Troy High School, Troy School District. Dr. Richard Machesky, Superintendent of Schools. Revised, February, 2025.

**Schools and contacts**
- Athens High School: Mr. Vernon Burden, Principal, 4333 John R. Road, Troy, Michigan 48085
- Troy High School: Mr. Remo Roncone, Principal, 4777 Northfield Parkway, Troy, Michigan 48098
- Department of Teaching & Learning, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.5221
- Title IX / Section 504 / ADA: John Pagel, Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, MI 48098-4799, (248)823-4000
- Central Office Special Education: 248.823.5096

**Nondiscrimination**
The policy cites Title IX of the Educational Amendments of 1972, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, and the Americans with Disabilities Act. Jordan M. Harris, J.D., Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, is the Title IX and Section 504/ADA Coordinator for employment and personnel matters; the Director of Special Education is the Section 504/ADA Coordinator for students.

**Graduation requirements (Class of 2025 and beyond)**

| Area | Required credits |
| --- | --- |
| English | 4.0 |
| Science | 3.0 |
| Mathematics | 4.0 |
| Social Studies | 3.0 |
| Personal Finance | 0.5 |
| Physical Education | 1.0 |
| Health | 0.5 |
| World Language, Fine & Applied Arts, CTE | 3.0 |
| Online Learning Experience | 0.0 |
| State Assessments | 0.0 |
| Total | 22.5 |

Personal Finance is embedded in Economics and becomes a requirement with the class of 2028. The online learning experience is a non-credit 20-hour requirement. Science differs by cohort: the classes of '27, '28 and '29 take Biology (1.0), Chemistry 1 (0.5) and Physics 1 (0.5), Environmental Science: Human Impact (0.5) and a science elective (0.5); the class of '26 takes Biology (1.0), Chemistry or Physics (1.0) and a science elective (1.0).

**Flexibility options** (updated 9.2015, MCL 380.1278a & MCL 380.1278b)
A Personal Curriculum aligned to the Educational Development Plan; waiver of the 0.5-credit Physical Education elective for two seasons of district athletics or marching band; World Language flexibility for heritage-language proficiency, international study, or substitution of CTE or Applied Arts credits; and CTE completion exchanged 1:1 for science, world language or Algebra 2 credit.

**Career and Technical Education**
Twelve programs: Architecture and Design; Automotive Technology; Business Administration, Management and Operations; Computer Programming; Computer Information Systems and Security; Culinary Arts; Education; Finance; Marketing and Sales; Mechanical Drafting (Woodworking); Mechatronics; and Radio and Broadcasting Technology. Completers take courses in sequential order; a C or better makes a student eligible for credentials including Certiport, Microsoft Office Specialist, ServSafe, ProStart and the Child Development Associate (CDA).

**Oakland Schools Technical Campus**
OSTC-SE, 5055 Delemere Street, Royal Oak, MI, serves grades 11-12 half-days. Morning classes begin 7:50 AM and dismiss 10:20 AM; the afternoon session runs 12:00 PM to 2:30 PM (08101 Session 1 AM, 08102 Session 2 PM). Credit is generally 1.5 credits per semester; if regular students carry six credits, OSTC students carry three at their home school plus three at OSTC. Applications close at the end of February, and OSTC credits are not NCAA approved.

**Grievance procedure**
A written grievance alleging discrimination on the basis of sex, race, color, religion, national origin, age (employees only), height, weight, marital status or handicap is filed with the Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services. Step 1 requires filing within 10 workdays, a meeting within 5 workdays and a written answer within 3 workdays; Steps 2 and 3 each allow 3 workdays to appeal, 10 workdays to meet and 5 workdays to answer, with the Superintendent's decision final and binding.
2025_133_course_description_book_2024_20.verbose:
**Publication and contacts.** The 2025-2026 Course Descriptions booklet covers Athens High School and Troy High School in the Troy School District, is issued under Dr. Richard Machesky, Superintendent of Schools, and is marked "Revised, February, 2025." Athens High School is listed with Principal Mr. Vernon Burden at 4333 John R. Road, Troy, Michigan 48085; Troy High School with Principal Mr. Remo Roncone at 4777 Northfield Parkway, Troy, Michigan 48098. Back matter lists the Department of Teaching & Learning at 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.5221, main offices 248.823.2900 and 248.823.2700, counseling 248.823.2962 and 248.823.2715, attendance 248.823.2901 and 248.823.2701, and Special Education at 248.823.5096.

**Nondiscrimination policy.** The opening policy cites Title IX of the Educational Amendments of 1972, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 and the Americans with Disabilities Act. Jordan M. Harris, J.D., Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, is named Title IX and Section 504/ADA Coordinator for employment and personnel matters; the Director of Special Education is Section 504/ADA Coordinator for handicapped and suspected handicapped students. Questions go to John Pagel, Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, MI 48098-4799, (248)823-4000.

**Graduation requirements.** Requirements are stated for the classes of 2025, 2026, 2027 and 2028, with total credits needed for graduation of 22.5 for a Troy High School or Troy Athens diploma. English requires 4.0 credits: English 9 1.0, English 10 1.0, English 11 Lit/Comp plus an elective or 11 English AP 1 & 2 1.0, and English 12 Lit/Comp or 12 English AP 1 & 2 1.0. Science requires 3.0 credits: the classes of ’27, ’28 and ’29 take Biology 1.0, Chemistry 1 0.5 and Physics 1 0.5, Environmental Science: Human Impact 0.5 and a science elective 0.5, while the class of ’26 takes Biology 1.0, Chemistry or Physics 1.0 and a science elective 1.0; AP Environmental Science (1.0) can replace Environmental Science: Human Impact (0.5). Mathematics requires 4.0 credits: Algebra 1 1.0, Geometry 1.0, Algebra 2 or Algebra 2 Part A and Part B 1.0 (also meetable through CTE program completion such as OSTC), and a math elective 1.0, with a math experience required in the final year. Social Studies requires 3.0 credits: World History/Geography 1 & 2 1.0, with AP Human Geography fulfilling World 1; American History/Geography 1 & 2 1.0; Economics 0.5; Government and Civics 0.5. Personal Finance is 0.5 credit embedded into Economics, required beginning with the class of 2028 and obtainable only through a TSD Economics or AP Economics course. Physical Education requires 1.0 credit and Health 0.5. World Language, Fine & Applied Arts and CTE requires 3.0 credits: 2.0 World Language credits, non-sequential accepted, or 1.0 World Language plus 1.0 CTE or VPAA, in addition to 1.0 VPAA. A 20-hour online learning experience and state assessments are non-credit requirements.

**Flexibility options.** Updated 9.2015 under MCL 380.1278a and MCL 380.1278b: a Personal Curriculum aligned to a student’s Educational Development Plan; excusal from the 0.5-credit Physical Education elective for two seasons of Troy School District athletics or marching band, tracked automatically with no forms required; World Language flexibility for heritage language proficiency, international study and residence, or substitution of CTE or Applied Arts credits; and CTE program completion exchanged 1:1 for science or world language credit or to satisfy Algebra 2.

**Career and Technical Education.** Twelve programs are listed: Architecture and Design; Automotive Technology; Business Administration, Management and Operations (BAMO); Computer Programming; Computer Information Systems and Security; Culinary Arts; Education; Finance; Marketing and Sales; Mechanical Drafting (Woodworking); Mechatronics; and Radio and Broadcasting Technology. Completers take required courses in sequential order, and a C or better in each course confers eligibility for an industry-certified credential.

**Business, marketing and work-based learning.** BAMO comprises 005231 Business Entrepreneurship, 005404 Digital Business and 005415 Business Law & Management, with Certiport Entrepreneurship and Small Business certification worth two ACE credits and a Communication Career Skills Artificial Intelligence certification worth one ACE credit. Finance and Accounting comprises 005011 Financial Accounting 1, 005012 Financial Accounting 2 and 005124 Building Wealth & Investments, each satisfying a half credit of the math-related graduation requirement in 12th grade. Marketing and Sales includes Marketing 1, Advanced Marketing, Sports and Entertainment Marketing, Marketing Research Capstone and School Based Enterprise, with DECA and the Troy Athens Fantasy League. Work-Based Learning students may earn up to 2.0 credits for work of at least 10 hours per week and 200 hours per semester; unpaid students must not exceed 45 hours per training experience.

**Technical and applied programs.** Information Technology covers Computer Programming, Cybersecurity and Digital/Multimedia, with AP Computer Science A, Computer Science Principles AP, Cybersecurity (003172 at Troy High, 103172/203172 at Athens), Web Creation and Game Design. Careers in Education 1 and 2, held at Athens using the Troy Athens Preschool, offer advanced placement credit at Central University, Western Michigan University, Oakland University, Macomb Community College and Davenport University plus a Child Development Associate (CDA) credential. Drafting and mechatronics offerings are Architectural Drawing 1 and 2, Woodworking Design & Fabrication 1 and 2, Engineering & Advanced Manufacturing and Engineering & Digital Manufacturing Systems. Automotive Technology at Troy High runs Auto Tech 1 through 4, with Auto Tech 2 a 2-hour block worth 1 credit per semester with 2 retakes, meeting NATEF Automotive Maintenance and Light Repair standards. Culinary Arts at Athens offers Restaurant Operations / Terrace Cafe (2 hours, 2 credits), Commercial Baking and Commercial Foods on the ProStart curriculum.

**English, ELD and Fine Arts.** English sequences are English 9, English 10, 11 English Literature/Composition or 11 English AP, and 12 English Lit/Comp or 12 English AP, with electives such as Creative Writing, Classical Mythology and Drama, Graphic Novels, Science Fiction, Speech, Debate and Writing for Publication. AP Seminar and AP Research culminate in a paper of approximately 4000-5000 words. ELD placement follows the State of Michigan Entrance Protocol with annual WIDA ACCESS testing, offering Beginner, Intermediate and Advanced ELD, Bridges to Lit/Comp for ELs and EL Tutorial, graded pass/fail. Fine Arts spans Drawing 1 through Advanced Art AP, Campus Band and Freshman Orchestra through Symphony Orchestra, Concert Choir and Madrigal Singers, Music Theory, which counts as a math elective credit for juniors and seniors who have completed all other required math credits, Intro to Music Technology and Recording using ProTools, and Theatre I through III.

**Mathematics, Health and Physical Education.** Mathematics runs from Algebra 1 and Intensified Algebra 1, a double-blocked 2-hour course worth 1 credit per semester, through Geometry, Algebra 2 with Part A and Part B variants, Precalculus, College Algebra, Calculus AB AP, Calculus BC AP, Statistics AP, Calculus 3 and Linear Algebra (dual enrollment with Lawrence Tech), Introduction to Data Science and Data Structures and Algorithms. Health offers 008852 Health, stated as required for graduation, and Peer Mediation; Multi-Departmental offers Innovation Learning and Innovation Lab, influenced by the "D school" at Stanford University, plus LEAP: Linking Education and People. Physical Education requires Intro to Physical Activity Level 1 (007952) or Level 2 (007962), including CPR training, fitness, swimming testing and team sports; Lifeguarding requires students to be 15 years old and costs $40 for Red Cross certification.

**Science, Social Studies, Special Education and World Language.** Science includes Biology, Anatomy and Physiology, Genetics/Bacteriology/Biotechnology/Embryology, Biology AP, Chemistry 1 and 2, AP Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Physics 1 and 2, Engineering Physics, AP Physics 2 and C, Environmental Science: Human Impact, Astronomy, Forensic Science and Environmental Science AP. Social Studies includes World History/Geography 1 and 2, Human Geography AP, American History/Geography, Economics, Government and Civics, Psychology, Sociology, Mental Health, Philosophy, Comparative Government and Politics AP built around China, Great Britain, Iran, Mexico, Nigeria and Russia, History through Film, Conflicts of the 20th & 21st Centuries, LINK, AP Art History covering 250 works of art, and Stories of Yourself & Others, carrying a half ELA credit and a half History credit. Special Education offers Integrated Studies, Linguistics and Composition, Reading Strategies, Integrated Math, English Language Arts, Math Skills A/B, Life Skills Math and LS sections of core subjects. World Language, keyed to the ACTFL Proficiency Guidelines, runs through level 4 in French, Spanish, Japanese, Chinese and German with AP courses in the first four; Japanese 2 students read and write 120 basic Kanji, Japanese 3 adds another 170+ and Japanese 4 another 180+.

**Oakland Schools Technical Campus.** OSTC-SE, the Southeast Campus at 5055 Delemere Street, Royal Oak, MI, north of 14 Mile between Crooks and Coolidge, serves grades 11-12 through half-day clusters staffed by instructors holding a Michigan Teaching Certificate and Vocational Authorization. Course numbers 08101 (Session 1 AM) and 08102 (Session 2 PM) correspond to a morning session beginning at 7:50 AM and dismissing at 10:20 AM and an afternoon session beginning at 12:00 PM and dismissing at 2:30 PM. Credit is generally 1.5 credits per semester; if regular students carry six (6) credits, OSTC students must carry three (3) credits at their home high school in addition to three (3) credits at OSTC. Offerings include Automotive Technology and, at the Pontiac Northeast Campus, Cosmetology, both of which must begin in 11th grade, plus Collision Repair, Computer Networking, Construction Technology, Culinary Arts/Hospitality, Health Sciences, Machining, Mechatronics, Visual Imaging Technology, Welding and Homeland Security. Students apply at www.ostconline.com by the end of February, and OSTC credits are not NCAA approved.

**Anti-discrimination grievance procedure.** Students or employees alleging discrimination on the basis of sex (including sexual harassment), race, color, religion, national origin, age (employees only), height, weight, marital status or handicap file a written grievance with the Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, the designated compliance administrator. Step 1 requires filing with the immediate supervisor within 10 workdays of the incident, a meeting within 5 workdays of filing and a written answer within 3 workdays. Step 2 allows appeal within 3 workdays, a meeting with the Assistant Superintendent or Deputy Superintendent within 10 workdays and an answer within 5 workdays; Step 3 follows the same intervals with the Superintendent, whose decision is final and binding. A grievance not filed or appealed within the time limits is deemed abandoned.
